{"mathdb_id": 338242, "uuid": "1bb02ef5-2a9b-4684-998d-09f4fe0da57e", "canonical_url": "https://mathdb.com/p/338242/emms-hancock-severini-wilson-conjecture-on-positive-supports", "title": "Emms–Hancock–Severini–Wilson conjecture on positive supports of Grover walks", "statement": "Let $G$ and $H$ be strongly regular graphs. Let $U_G$ and $U_H$ denote the time evolution operators of the Grover walks induced by $G$ and $H$, respectively, and for a real matrix $M$ let $S(M)$ be its positive support, defined by

$$
S(M)_{b,a}=\begin{cases}1&\text{if }M_{b,a}>0,\\0&\text{if }M_{b,a}\leq 0.\end{cases}
$$
 Let $\sigma(M)$ denote the spectrum of a matrix $M$.

**Emms–Hancock–Severini–Wilson conjecture.**

$$
G\cong H\Longleftrightarrow\sigma\bigl(S(U_G^3)\bigr)=\sigma\bigl(S(U_H^3)\bigr).
$$

The conjecture proposes that the spectrum of the positive support of the cube of the Grover-walk operator distinguishes non-isomorphic strongly regular graphs, and is motivated by the connection between Grover-walk positive supports, graph spectra, and graph isomorphism. $$
\varphi_4(S_{4,2^sm+2^{s-1}}(n))=\varphi_4(S_{4,2^{s-1}}(n)).
